title: Expand generated API-reference coverage: all real TypeScript projects + all Rust workspace crates
objective: Owner-directed follow-up to G-DOCS-TYPEDOC-API-REFERENCE: the owner confirmed two scope expansions (TypeDoc across all real TypeScript projects, not just @grafting/ui and @grafting/x6-canvas; and generalizing the existing per-crate Rustdoc-JSON pattern in libs/graph/core, today used only for its own public-API drift check, to all six real Cargo workspace members). Explicit owner intent: this evidence is meant primarily to help AI agents work the codebase (compact, structured, always-fresh ground truth instead of re-grepping source), human browsing is secondary. This record is a placeholder for pre-implementation recon (toolchain availability, per-project entry-point shape) before committing to a concrete plan; not yet claimed in_progress.
validations: rustup toolchain list: nightly-2025-11-23 (the pinned toolchain in tools/rust-public-api-toolchain.txt) already installed -- no environment change needed

TypeScript: expanded generate-api-docs.mjs to 4 targets (ui, x6-canvas, isekai-web-client, architecture-studio via explicit internal-module entry points, since it has no package.json main/types export); packages/isekai-wasm deliberately excluded (compiled wasm-bindgen output only, no hand-written src/). All 4 convert and --check converges.

Real bug found and fixed mid-task: the first Rust implementation shelled directly to `cargo rustdoc --output-format json` and committed the RAW Rustdoc JSON model -- grafting-domain-core.json alone was 1.5 MB, because rustdoc's own JSON index carries one entry per impl block (confirmed by inspecting a sample item). Directly contradicted the owner's stated goal ('ajudar mais a IA'). Owner chose the fix: generalize the curation libs/graph/core/tests/public_api_snapshot.rs already proves (Rustdoc JSON + public-api crate, omit_blanket_impls) into a new shared tool instead of committing raw rustdoc output or hand-rolling a JS filter.

New tools/rust-api-docgen binary crate (workspace member) built clean: `cargo build -p grafting-rust-api-docgen` and `cargo check --locked --workspace` both succeed, including alongside all pre-existing crates.

Re-ran generation after the fix: total Rust output shrank from 2.4 MB to 234 KB across 6 crates (grafting-domain-core.json: 1.5 MB -> 132 KB); sizes now comparable to the TypeScript side (91-97 KB each).
node tools/scripts/generate-api-docs.mjs --check and generate-rust-api-docs.mjs --check: both converge clean immediately after generation, for all 4 TS + 6 Rust targets

Real drift proof on both sides (same pattern as prior tasks): hand-corrupted docs/generated/api/rust/grafting-graph-core.json (added a stray top-level key) -> --check failed naming the stale file -> regenerated -> --check passed again
pnpm run docs:check: full 7-step chain passes end to end (graph:map/manifest/extract:check, docs:api:ts:check, docs:api:rust:check, graph-core:api-check, x6-canvas:api-check)

git status --short: only this task's declared affected_paths changed (plus Cargo.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml from new dependencies), confirmed alongside other pre-existing uncommitted work from earlier in this session
artifacts: tools/rust-api-docgen/ (new Cargo workspace member: curated public-API JSON extractor, reused by all 6 Rust crates)
tools/scripts/generate-api-docs.mjs (now 4 TS targets, output moved to docs/generated/api/ts/)
tools/scripts/generate-rust-api-docs.mjs (now shells to tools/rust-api-docgen instead of raw cargo rustdoc)
tools/scripts/README.md (new sections for both extractors and the shared Rust tool)
risks: packages/isekai-wasm has no hand-written src/ -- it is compiled wasm-bindgen output (own package.json says 'No domain logic here'); TypeDoc over it would just restate generated bindings, not real signal. Proposed to exclude, pending owner confirmation.

apps/architecture-studio is an app, not a library -- no package.json main/types/exports entry point the way packages/isekai-web-client has. Documenting it needs TypeDoc's multi-file 'expand' entry-point strategy over its internal modules instead of a single public entry point -- a different flavor (internal architecture map, not public API surface).

Rust coverage requires the pinned nightly-2025-11-23 toolchain (tools/rust-public-api-toolchain.txt) that only libs/graph/core's ignored public_api_snapshot.rs test currently uses. Installing a new toolchain via rustup is a real environment change (network download, disk space) if it is not already present -- confirming installed state before proceeding, not installing unprompted.

The existing Rust pattern duplicates rustdoc_json/public_api Builder boilerplate directly inside libs/graph/core's own test file; generalizing to six crates as six more near-duplicate test files would be real duplication. A single shared script/tool (mirroring how generate-api-docs.mjs already handles multiple TS packages from one script) is the better shape, pending owner confirmation this is worth the larger surface.
